name: DeLorean DMC-12
assembly: Dunmurry, Northern Ireland (DeLorean Motor Cars, Ltd.)

height.sourceNote: Doors closed; with the gull-wing doors raised, height at the door tops is 1962 mm.

power.sourceNote: 130 bhp at 5,500 rpm, explicitly labelled bhp (mechanical horsepower) in the source's technical-data table, converted at 1 hp = 0.745699872 kW (96.9 kW, rounded to 97).

torque.sourceNote: The article's body text and infobox both state 153 lb-ft at 2,750 rpm, citing Espey 2014 (207.4 N⋅m, rounded to 207), the figure recorded here. The article's own technical-data table, citing period Road & Track and Car and Driver tests, separately states 162 lb-ft (219.6 N⋅m) at the same 2,750 rpm for the same engine. The two are not reconciled or averaged.

topSpeed.sourceNote: DMC's claimed top speed of 130 mph, converted at 1 mph = 1.609344 km/h (209.2 km/h, rounded to 209). Road & Track measured a considerably lower 110 mph (177 km/h) and described the car as 'not quick for a sports/GT car in this price category'; the manufacturer-claimed figure is recorded here, with the tested figure noted rather than substituted.

hero.alt: Stainless-steel DeLorean DMC-12 photographed head-on with both gull-wing doors raised
hero.caption: The gull-wing doors, raised on their cryogenically-treated torsion bars. They are one of the DMC-12's few genuinely novel features.

gallery.alt: Silver DeLorean DMC-12 photographed from the rear three-quarter angle at a car show, showing its unpainted brushed-steel body panels and slatted rear window louvres
gallery.caption: The bare stainless-steel panels were rust-proof and never painted at the factory, which is why every DMC-12 looks the same colour.
